records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts (148.256, 2 of 8 correct) failed the same way: six runs never wrote any explicit candidate list, instead oscillating in prose between the two readings of the public number and re-arguing the same paragraph, with four hitting the generation cap and emitting no boxed answer. The two winners were the only runs that eventually enumerated candidates line by line. Meanwhile no rollout in this or the last four rounds ever used the incumbent clause about not reasoning from the original set, and repeated pure compressions of that clause (rounds 8, 11, 12) all lost held-out. So this edit keeps every piece of machinery the winners used, drops that inert clause, spends the saved tokens naming the concrete first move the losers lack (write the list out before arguing), and makes the terminal action boxing the survivor.

Fresh rollouts (148.257) scored 8/8, so train is saturated and only transfer matters. All eight traces reached w on a fixed circle and inverted the map fast, then stalled on the vague "characterize the image locus" step: every one parametrized w by an angle, computed |z| as a function of that angle, and looped on the fact that root moduli are not constant (one burned 11845 tokens). The three fastest traces escaped only by pushing the |w|=R condition back onto z as a distance relation. This edit names that conversion as the concrete next move, so the student never enters the angle parametrization. History says pure compression is exhausted (rounds 5, 11, 12 lost) and appended guards lost, so the untested lever is making the one vague clause executable at equal length: 70 tokens, same as the incumbent.

Rollouts scored 4/8. Two failures were method failures of the same kind: each asserted an overlap value in prose (one claimed the shared region vanishes, one claimed a floor for it) without ever solving for a single boundary crossing, then boxed the resulting total. The other two ran the budget out on tilted placements. The incumbent's remedy for this is a bare prohibition plus the word 'extent', which appeared 0-2 times per trace while coordinates appeared 15-31 times, so it is inert. This edit replaces that prohibition with the positive executable move the four successes actually made - solve for where the boundaries cross and read the overlap off those points - which applies to any overlap, union or region-area problem, and lands at 168 tokens versus the incumbent's 169.

Fresh round-13 rollouts (148.259) scored 6/8. Both failures are token-ceiling truncations with the same cause: they never form the partition, so they keep re-asking whether a high-degree polynomial can serve a whole stretch, and finally report a single factor (the per-polynomial capacity, or the menu size) instead of the total. All six correct rollouts talk about blocks heavily; the two failures barely mention them, so the closing clause is the load-bearing step and its current wording ('attain it by letting each polynomial match L on its own block') is too vague to execute. This edit spends words on the concrete constructive move - split the inputs into consecutive blocks of deg P, one per polynomial - and names the product to box, while keeping every earlier step and coming in shorter than the incumbent (139 vs 146 tokens).

5/8 correct. The three failures are separated from the five successes by one measurable behaviour: each failure switched to decimal approximations (35, 105 and 143 numeric estimates) after reaching an awkward root, then spent the rest of the budget comparing approximate candidate values and never boxed anything; every success stayed in fractions and finished under 27k characters. Meanwhile the incumbent's 'a zero or impossible intermediate means relabel, not restart' clause appears in zero rollouts across every round I have, so it is inert transfer tax. This edit spends those tokens on a positive, executable instruction to stay in exact fractions, which should generalise to any unseen problem where an approximation invites an endless numeric search instead of a committed answer, and it is shorter than the incumbent (67 vs 70 tokens).

3/8 correct. Every failure mishandled the buried-item part: three rollouts asserted each item is equally likely to arrive first or last and quoted 1/k, one priced a run only two moves long, and one declared the outcome impossible. The incumbent already says the destination's bottom arrived first, and one rollout used that, but none drew the missing consequence that a buried item can only arrive first after everything stacked above it has been moved, so the deciding prefix is several steps, not one choice. I add that consequence as a short clause and drop the sum-to-one branch check, which zero of eight rollouts executed here and in rounds 9-12. Net token count is unchanged, so the edit trades inert text for the fact the failures lacked.

Fresh round-13 rollouts scored 0/8. Six hit the 16384-token cap with no boxed value, and the mechanism in the two that finished is new and precise: both reached a correct structural setup, then extracted the requested coefficient from it with an unjustified step and committed to that value without ever testing it against a small case - one had already computed a small case and dismissed it as inconsistent rather than using it as a check. The incumbent closing clause is measurably inert: no rollout attempts a fourth size and lowercase confirm appears zero times in all eight traces. So I spend those tokens on the back-check the finishers were one step from doing - test the derived rule against the entries already recorded - and pay for it by merging the twin prohibitions, a rewording round 11 showed is held-out-neutral. Same 70 tokens as the incumbent.

All three failures in my 8 rollouts followed the hint correctly through the gcd step, listed the admissible divisor candidates, then abandoned that list and substituted the stated grouping count as the item count on a bare plausibility argument; the five successes instead summed the stage totals, divided once by a candidate, and applied the markup as a multiplier on cost. Explicit largest-admissible tiebreaks (rounds 2, 6) and plausibility prohibitions (round 4) all bought training and lost held-out, so instead I restore the two concrete computational moves the successes actually used - sum-then-divide-once ordering and naming the percent's base as cost rather than price - which co-occurred with this hint's best-ever held-out, and I pay for them by lexical compression so the hint is no longer than the incumbent and the grouping clause the successes rely on stays intact.

3/8 rollouts were correct and all finished normally near 10-12k tokens; the 5 failures every one hit the 16384-token cap while re-litigating WHAT the involution links, trying q(x)=p(s-x), then q=s-p(x)+k, then guessing s by trial, or falling back to full coefficient expansion. That is the same wall seen every round since round 2, and my manifest shows all six semantic fixes for it (explicit s formula, centered odd-power form, expand-identity-alone, three evaluation moves, direct f=s-g notation, half-budget rule) each LOST held-out. So this round is a strictly lossless compression instead: every content phrase is byte-identical and only two function-word choices change (and require -> requiring; a single -> one), for 147 -> 145 tokens. It cannot raise transfer, but it converts a held-out tie into a win, which is how the last four keeps in this book happened.

Fresh rollouts scored 2/8 and five of six failures hit the 16384-token cap with one shape: each measured the two smallest sizes by writing states, then abandoned measuring for a symbolic cycle-order argument, generated several contradicting candidate periods, and kept trying to justify one rather than commit - one recited the composite clause three times and still read the period off transpositions; none boxed anything. Both successes stopped the moment a pattern fit their measured sizes and boxed immediately. So the incumbent's closing 'check it reproduces every row, and box it rather than listing rivals' is too weak: it never tells the student that agreement with the measured rows is sufficient licence to stop. I replace it with an explicit stop rule, keep the table and composite clauses the successes rely on, and hold length at the incumbent's exact 102 tokens.
